# Feature: wink-nlp Local-Analysis Spike & Quick Wins

## 1. Feature Goal

**ID**: FEAT-WI-003
**Source Plan**: `.spec-lite/plan_web_intelligence.md`

Make the deterministic (`--no-llm`) flow measurably more helpful using **only** wink-nlp's local analysis (no new dependencies — `compromise` and transformers.js were previously declined). A bounded spike documents what wink-nlp offers beyond current usage; three quick wins then ship behind the `TextAnalyzer` port: a **negation-aware merge guard** (never merge a claim with its negation), **sentiment-based opinion handling** (keep strongly opinionated sentences out of `Key facts`), and a **readability-based junk gate** (reject boilerplate/gibberish that current heuristics miss). Each win ships only if the golden-corpus diff demonstrates improvement; regressions get documented in TODO instead of shipped.

## 2. Data Model (Granular)

No persisted data. The analyzer port's in-memory contract extends additively:

```ts
// text-analyzer.ts — AnalyzedSentence gains two fields (all implementations):
interface AnalyzedSentence {
  // ...existing index/text/tokens/lemmas...
  /** True when the sentence carries negation (wink `negationFlag`; baseline: false). */
  readonly negated: boolean;
  /** Sentence sentiment in [-1, 1] (wink `sentiment`; baseline: 0). */
  readonly sentiment: number;
}

// DocAnalysis gains a per-sentence junk signal (spike refines the exact inputs):
interface DocAnalysis {
  // ...existing sentences/entities/hasFiniteVerb...
  /** Composite readability/junk score for a sentence, [0,1]; higher = more junk-like. */
  junkScore(sentenceIndex: number): number;
}
```

`EvidenceClaim` carries the source sentence's `negated`/`sentiment` values forward (fields on the claim, populated at claim-candidate construction) so merge/gating stages don't re-analyze text.

## Spike Findings

> TASK-001 deliverable — surveyed 2026-07-18 against the installed `wink-nlp@2.4.0` + `wink-eng-lite-web-model@1.8.1`, with an empirical probe run through the shared engine configuration. Every decision below was verified against the actual package source (`src/wink-nlp.js`, `src/its.js`, `src/api/itm-sentence-out.js`) and live output, not just documentation.

### How wink-nlp's extra annotations work (mechanics)

- Sentences (and the document) are stored internally as `[start, end, negationFlag, sentimentScore]` tuples. The `negation` and `sentiment` pipe stages populate slots 2 and 3; without those stages the slots stay `0`.
- `sentence.out(its.negationFlag)` returns the **sentence-level** boolean directly from the tuple (special-cased in `itm-sentence-out.js`), and `sentence.out(its.sentiment)` returns the tuple's score. Both are O(1) reads after the pipe runs — no re-analysis.
- Pipe stages are independent flags: extending `PIPE` to `['sbd','pos','ner','cer','negation','sentiment']` adds the two automata passes per `readDoc` with no change to the existing sbd/pos/ner/cer output. The shared-engine pattern is unaffected (the pipe is fixed at engine construction; nothing becomes mutable).

### Candidate survey and decisions

**1. Sentence negation (`its.negationFlag`, pipe stage `negation`) — SHIP (TASK-003).**
Probe results: "Sales did not rise in 2025." → `true`; "Sales never rose in 2025." → `true`; "The company said it would not repeat the mistake." → `true`; affirmative counterparts → `false`. Reliable at sentence scope. Plugs into `shouldMerge` in `evidence-set.ts` as a polarity guard: lemma cosine of "Sales rose 12%" vs "Sales did not rise" is high (near-identical lemma bags — `not` is a stopword and vanishes from the bag), so today they can merge; the flag is exactly the missing signal. Expected corpus effect: no diff on the seven corpora unless a negation near-pair exists — a targeted fixture is added in TASK-003 to pin the behavior.

**2. Sentence sentiment (`its.sentiment`, pipe stage `sentiment`) — SHIP (TASK-004), with a documented threshold caveat.**
Probe results (score granularity ≈ 0.1, range [-1, 1]): "This is a fantastic, must-buy EV with amazing range." → `0.7`; "The report was terrible and disappointing for investors." → `-0.7`; "Sales rose 12% in 2025." → `0.2`; "EV sales in India reached 1.3 million units in 2024." → `0.2`; empty text → `0`. **Caveat discovered:** the AFINN-style lexicon fires on domain-neutral words — "Norway are one win from the semi-final." scores `0.8` because of "win". A `0.5` threshold would demote legitimate sports facts in the `worldcup-hubs` corpus. **Pinned design: start the gate at `|sentiment| > 0.6` (exclusive), evaluate the golden diff, and keep the demote-don't-drop rule strictly** — a demoted claim stays eligible for findings/`Additional findings`, so even a false-positive demotion never deletes a cited claim. If the worldcup diff still degrades, raise to 0.7 before falling back to the TODO route.

**3. Readability junk signal — SHIP (TASK-005) as a derived per-sentence `junkScore`; raw `readabilityStats` REJECTED at sentence scope.**
`its.readabilityStats` is **document-scoped** (needs the model's `readabilityStats` addon, which the lite web model has): it returns doc-level FRES, complex-word counts, and reading time. Probe: junk chrome text scores FRES 19 vs 62 for prose — the direction is right but the granularity is wrong; a per-sentence FRES would need syllable estimation we'd have to reimplement. **Pinned design — `junkScore(sentenceIndex)` is computed from per-token signals wink already exposes (`its.shape`, `its.stopWordFlag`, `its.pos`, `its.normal`), all deterministic:**

- Over the sentence's word tokens (POS not in {PUNCT, SYM, SPACE, X}):
  - `capRatio` — fraction of non-initial words whose `shape` starts with `X` (nav/title chrome is Title-Case-dense);
  - `stopDeficit` — `max(0, 1 − stopRatio / 0.25)` where `stopRatio` is the stopword fraction (real prose ≈ 0.2–0.6 stopwords; link glue has ~0);
  - `longRatio` — fraction of words with `normal.length ≥ 12` (SEO/gibberish glue);
- `junkScore = min(1, 0.5·capRatio + 0.4·stopDeficit + 0.1·longRatio)`; `0` for empty sentences.
- Probe separation on 7 junk / 7 prose fixtures: junk scores 0.45–0.90 ("Home News Sport…" 0.90, "Privacy Policy Terms of Use…" 0.45), prose 0.00–0.27 (worst: "Electric vehicle registrations declined slightly in March." 0.27). **Pinned eligibility threshold: reject at `junkScore > 0.4`** — clears the worst prose by a 0.18 margin while catching every junk fixture. Validated against `ev-sales-messy` / `worldcup-hubs` goldens in TASK-005. _(TASK-005 tuning outcome: 0.4 proved too aggressive on the real corpora — legitimate brand-word-dense prose such as "Rail operators scheduled 150 extra trains for FIFA World Cup supporters" scores ≈ 0.41 and lost cited claims from `worldcup-hubs`. The shipped threshold is `0.5`, which keeps every legitimate corpus claim while still rejecting SEO/nav glue, which measures 0.60+.)_

**4. `its.shape` / `its.stem` accessors — shape SHIPS as a `junkScore` input (above); stem REJECTED.**
`stem` (Porter2, via the model addon) is redundant with the lemmas the analyzer already exposes — no consumer needs a second, cruder normal form.

**5. Custom-entity recognition (`learnCustomEntities`) — REJECTED for this feature; already tracked in TODO.**
CER training mutates the engine, so it would require abandoning the shared immutable engine (or a second engine instance ≈ re-parsing the multi-MB model per configuration). The existing TODO entry ("wink-nlp CER for sharper figure/range/unit extraction", Web Intelligence section) stands; this spike adds no new evidence that the cost is worth it now — the lite model's NER + PROPN runs already cover the corpora's entity needs.

**6. `its.sentenceWiseImportance` — TODO (out of scope, newly recorded).**
Doc-scoped importance ranking (0–1 per sentence) that could complement the salience formula's position/overlap weighting. Not in this feature's scope (salience changes would churn every golden at once and are not one of the three pinned wins); recorded in `.spec-lite/TODO.md`.

### TASK-002 design answers (pinned)

- **Pipe stages**: `['sbd', 'pos', 'ner', 'cer', 'negation', 'sentiment']` — order irrelevant to wink (flags, not a sequence), keep the existing four first for readability.
- **`negated`**: `sentence.out(its.negationFlag) === true`. Baseline stub: `false`.
- **`sentiment`**: `Number(sentence.out(its.sentiment))`. Baseline stub: `0`.
- **`junkScore(i)`**: the formula in §3 above, computed inside `WinkAnalyzer.analyze` per sentence (same single pass that builds tokens/lemmas) and stored alongside `finiteVerbBySentence`. Baseline stub: `0`. Out-of-range index: `0`.
- **Sentiment gate threshold (TASK-004)**: `SENTIMENT_OPINION_THRESHOLD = 0.6` (exclusive compare, demote-don't-drop).
- **Junk gate threshold (TASK-005)**: `JUNK_SCORE_THRESHOLD = 0.4` (exclusive compare, reject at eligibility) — **revised to `0.5` during TASK-005 corpus tuning** (see the tuning-outcome note in §3 above).
